title: Read-only reviewers see a stale .beads/issues.jsonl and report live beads as non-existent
outcome:
Found by round-8 reviewers being WRONG in an instructive way.

Both delegated read-only reviewers ran 'bd show <id>' / 'bd search', which ERRORED in the child session. They fell back to grepping .beads/issues.jsonl — the passive export — and concluded that tm-xx3 'does not exist' and that the shared_codex.rs test-file split was 'untracked'. Both beads exist and are open (tm-xx3, tm-g41). The export was 2 DAYS stale (mtime 2026-07-10; the beads were created 2026-07-12).

Claude escalated this into a Medium finding — 'the acknowledged debt is untracked, and the placeholder reads as real' — i.e. it accused a code comment of citing a fake bead id. The comment was correct and the reviewer was not.

WHY IT MATTERS: a reviewer that cannot see the tracker produces confident false findings, and 'this bead is fake' is exactly the kind of finding a human acts on. It also silently inverts the value of citing bead ids in comments.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) make bd queryable from read-only reviewer children (it is a read; find why it errors — likely a Dolt lock or cwd/env issue), and/or (b) re-export .beads/issues.jsonl on write so the passive export cannot lag by days, and/or (c) tell reviewers explicitly that issues.jsonl is a passive export and NOT the source of truth.
